steps.subject: A faster path for the {company} team
steps.body:
Hi {firstName},

I've been tracking what's shifting at {company} this quarter, and the timing looked worth a note.

Teams at your stage usually lose eleven hours a week per rep to list building before a single conversation starts.

We got that under two for a peer team by consolidating enrichment into one workflow.

Worth fifteen minutes to see whether the same math holds at {company}?

details.title: Email Type
details.value: Cold outbound

details.title: Reasoning
details.value: Opens on the account signal rather than a generic introduction, quantifies what the current workflow costs, and closes with an ask sized to a first touch.

steps.subject: 8 tools, one list build
steps.body:
Hi Marcus,

Cirrus's outbound stack runs through ZoomInfo, Apollo, Clay, Outreach, Demandbase, and Lusha — at minimum. Your cross-sell SDRs are toggling between all of them just to build a single target list.

That's the #1 productivity drain we hear from SDR managers at this scale — reps spend more time sourcing across fragmented tools than actually selling.

Bluebirds consolidates enrichment across 15 data vendors into one platform. 30-min Salesforce setup, no new UI for reps to learn.

Can I share a 2-min walkthrough of the platform running a cross-sell list build?

details.title: Email Type
details.value: Warm outbound

details.title: Reasoning
details.value: Names all six tools instead of gesturing at sprawl, so the opening proves the research rather than claiming it. The ask is a two-minute walkthrough, not a meeting, which keeps the first reply cheap.

Bluebirds gives your SDR managers the same power without depending on eng. Time-to-value for the DACH launch: days, not quarters.

Worth twenty minutes before that team is seated?

steps.subject: Onboarding 12 SDRs a month — ramp is where it slips
steps.body:
Hi Patrick,

Harbour Capital is onboarding ten to twelve SDRs every month. Good signal on the trajectory.

The part that catches sales leaders off guard isn't the hiring — it's the ramp. Bringing on a dozen at once, new reps lose fifteen hours a week to manual research while enablement is still catching up on last quarter's changes.

We helped a peer revenue org shorten ramp by 30% without adding enablement headcount.

Open to a short conversation before the class starts?
